questions.q:
In the context of water governance in India, consider the following statements:
1. The Constitution places water in the Concurrent List.
2. The Composite Water Management Index, which ranks States on water management, is compiled by the Central Water Commission.
3. The Jal Jeevan Mission aims at functional tap connections for urban households.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: None is correct. Water is Entry 17 of the State List, subject to the Union's power over inter-State rivers under Entry 56 of the Union List, so statement 1 fails. The Composite Water Management Index is a NITI Aayog benchmarking exercise; the Central Water Commission deals with surface water, river-basin planning and flood control. The Jal Jeevan Mission of 2019 is for rural households and has been extended to 2028; urban supply is covered by AMRUT.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: In India, coal's share in electricity actually generated is far higher than its share in installed capacity.
Statement-II: Solar and wind plants run at much lower capacity utilisation than coal plants because their output is intermittent.
Statement-III: India does not yet have enough grid-scale battery and pumped-hydro storage to shift renewable output to hours of peak demand.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-II and Statement-III are correct and both of them explain Statement-I
Both Statement-II and Statement-III are correct but only one of them explains Statement-I
Only one of the Statements II and III is correct and that explains Statement-I
Neither Statement-II nor Statement-III is correct
questions.e: Both later statements are correct and both explain the first. By March 2026 renewables and coal each had a little over two-fifths of installed capacity, yet in April 2026 coal produced about 72 per cent of electricity. A megawatt of solar or wind produces far fewer units in a year than a megawatt of coal, and without storage the evening peak still has to be met by coal. Capacity is not generation.

questions.q:
With reference to dam safety arrangements in India, consider the following pairs:
Body or tool : Role
1. National Committee on Dam Safety : Apex body in the structure created by the Dam Safety Act, 2021
2. National Dam Safety Authority : Regulator that implements the Act
3. State Dam Safety Organisation : Surveillance and inspection of dams at the State level
4. DHARMA : Platform using artificial intelligence and sensors for real-time flood forecasting at dams and barrages
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correct and describe three of the four tiers under the 2021 Act; the fourth is the State Committee on Dam Safety. Pair 4 is wrong. DHARMA, introduced in the first phase of the rehabilitation project, is a digital record of dam health, inspections and maintenance. Real-time monitoring and flood forecasting with artificial intelligence and sensors is the function of a separate tool, eAabhas.

questions.q: In weather and climate forecasting, 'downscaling' refers to
o: shortening the lead time of a forecast to improve its accuracy
averaging forecasts of several models to remove their individual errors
deriving fine-resolution local forecasts from the output of coarser models
reducing the number of weather stations needed to run a model
questions.e: Global and regional models work on grids many kilometres wide, too coarse for a village or city ward. Downscaling translates that output into finer detail, either with a nested high-resolution model or statistically; AI methods learn the link between coarse fields and local observations. It does not cut the observation network, and it differs from ensemble averaging. Hyper-local forecasts help farm decisions, flood warnings and urban heat planning.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Report)
A. State and Trends of Carbon Pricing
B. Global Forest Goals Report
C. Global Forest Resources Assessment
D. Emissions Gap Report
List-II (Brought out by)
1. Food and Agriculture Organization
2. UN Environment Programme
3. World Bank
4. UN Department of Economic and Social Affairs
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: The World Bank's annual carbon-pricing report in 2026 noted India's entry as a large carbon market. The Global Forest Goals Report comes from the UN's economic and social affairs department through the secretariat of the UN Forum on Forests, and tracks the six voluntary forest goals. It is often confused with the FAO's five-yearly forest resources assessment, which supplies the area data. The Emissions Gap Report is UNEP's.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 80; Vision IAS pp. 82-83; FAO and UNEP reports are static

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Coal gasification is described as an interim bridge for India and not as a clean end-state.
Statement-II: Products made from syngas carry no carbon dioxide emissions over their life cycle because the coal is not burnt.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is not. Gasification avoids direct combustion and yields carbon dioxide in a concentrated stream that is easier to capture, yet the carbon in the coal still ends up as emissions unless captured, and capture technology remains costly and has underperformed. The process also uses a lot of water. Its attraction is import substitution for methanol, fertiliser inputs and gas, which is why it is called a bridge.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the Small Hydro Power Development Scheme approved in 2026 is correct?
o: It funds only storage-based projects, since run-of-the-river plants cannot give firm power.
It provides assistance only for preparing project reports and not for building plants.
It is implemented by the Ministry of Power as part of its large-hydro programme.
It supports projects of 1 MW to 25 MW, with a higher rate of assistance for the North-Eastern States and international border districts.
questions.e: The scheme runs for five years from 2026-27 under the renewable energy ministry, which handles hydro up to 25 MW; larger projects fall under the power ministry. Assistance per megawatt and the ceiling per project are higher in the North-East and border districts than elsewhere. Small hydro is mostly run-of-the-river, using natural flow without large storage. Project-report support is one component, alongside capital assistance.

questions.q:
Consider the following big cats covered by the International Big Cat Alliance, which Saudi Arabia joined in 2026:
1. Tiger
2. Snow leopard
3. Cheetah
4. Puma
How many of the above are classified as 'Endangered' on the IUCN Red List?
questions.e: Only the tiger is Endangered. The snow leopard was moved from Endangered to Vulnerable in 2017, and the cheetah as a species is Vulnerable, though its Asiatic subspecies in Iran is Critically Endangered. The puma is of Least Concern. Among the seven cats under the alliance, the lion and leopard are also Vulnerable and the jaguar is Near Threatened. Five of the seven occur in India; the jaguar and puma do not.

questions.q:
With reference to terms associated with the SEHAT initiative, consider the following statements:
1. Biofortification means adding micronutrients to food at the stage of processing or milling.
2. 'One Health' refers to an integrated approach to health at the interface of humans, animals and the environment.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 describes food fortification, such as adding iron to flour or iodine to salt. Biofortification raises the nutrient content of the crop itself, through conventional breeding, agronomic practice or biotechnology, without loss of yield traits; zinc-rich wheat and iron-rich pearl millet are examples. Statement 2 is correct. One Health links human, animal and environmental health through shared surveillance and research, and is one of the five priorities of the initiative.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 77-78; fortification contrast is static

questions.q:
Arrange the following in chronological order, from the earliest to the latest:
1. Adoption of the Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court
2. Vietnam writes ecocide into its domestic law
3. UN Conference on the Human Environment at Stockholm
4. ENMOD Convention on hostile use of environmental modification comes into force
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Stockholm came first, in 1972, where the Swedish Prime Minister used the word ecocide for the Vietnam War. The ENMOD Convention followed, coming into force in 1978 as a reaction to the same war. Vietnam made ecocide a domestic crime in 1990. The Rome Statute was adopted in 1998 with only four core crimes. The sequence shows the idea grew out of the Vietnam War but has stayed outside international criminal law.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 49-50; the 1998 date is static

questions.q:
With reference to coal gasification and the incentive scheme approved by the Union Cabinet in 2026, consider the following statements:
1. Syngas consists mainly of carbon monoxide and hydrogen.
2. Gasification means burning coal completely in excess air to produce a fuel gas.
3. Fluidised-bed gasifiers are favoured in India because domestic coal has a very high ash content.
4. The scheme confines support to a single imported gasifier technology.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Gasification is a thermo-chemical process in which crushed coal reacts with limited oxygen and steam at high temperature and pressure, giving a mixture of carbon monoxide and hydrogen; it is not complete combustion, so statement 2 is wrong. Indian coal carries 30 to 45 per cent ash, which makes many foreign gasifiers unworkable. Statement 4 is wrong: the scheme is technology-agnostic and chooses projects by competitive bidding.

questions.q: Which one of the following best describes the National Water Policy, 2012?
o: A non-binding policy guide that stresses integrated management and treats water as an economic good
A law made by Parliament under Entry 56 of the Union List to regulate inter-State rivers
A set of statutory rules under the Water Act, 1974 that fixes water charges for industry
An index of NITI Aayog that ranks States on their management of water
questions.e: The 2012 policy is a strategic statement without legal force. It asks for integrated, basin-level management and conservation, and says that water beyond basic needs should be priced as an economic good. It is not a law under Entry 56, which is the basis of the River Boards Act, nor a rule under the pollution law. The ranking of States is done separately by NITI Aayog's water index.

questions.q:
With reference to India's circular-economy framework, consider the following statements:
1. The Circular Economy Cell that coordinates this agenda is located in the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.
2. The Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022 prohibit disposal of waste batteries by landfilling and incineration.
3. Extended Producer Responsibility is moving from targets based on collection to targets based on recycling.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is wrong: the Circular Economy Cell sits in NITI Aayog, which is one reason the recycling industry complains that no single ministry owns the subject. Statement 2 is right; the 2022 battery rules set collection, recycling and refurbishment targets and bar landfilling and incineration. Statement 3 is right; EPR is being redesigned so that producers are judged on material actually recycled, not merely collected.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Platform : Description
1. Petersberg Climate Dialogue : Formal negotiating session of the subsidiary bodies of the UNFCCC
2. Santa Marta Conference on Transitioning Away from Fossil Fuels : Body that replaces UNFCCC negotiations on fossil fuels
3. Science Panel for the Global Energy Transition : Working group of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: None of the pairs is correct. The Petersberg Dialogue is an informal ministerial meeting begun by Germany in 2010; its 2026 edition was the first big climate ministerial of the year. The Santa Marta conference, co-hosted by Colombia and the Netherlands, is a political platform for implementation and explicitly neither negotiates nor replaces the UN process. The science panel was launched at Santa Marta to suggest country and sector milestones, outside the IPCC.

questions.q:
With reference to the Methane Alert and Response System (MARS), consider the following statements:
1. It is run by the International Methane Emissions Observatory of the UN Environment Programme and uses satellite data to notify very large methane leaks.
2. In 2026 its coverage was extended beyond oil and gas facilities to coal mines and waste sites.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both are correct. The system was launched at COP27 in 2022 as the first public, global, satellite-based system to detect and notify super-emitters. It began with oil and gas facilities linked to a UNEP industry partnership and now also covers coal mines and waste facilities; it flagged a Mumbai landfill among the largest emitting sites. It supports the Global Methane Pledge on cutting methane this decade.

questions.q: In steelmaking, syngas obtained from coal gasification is of interest chiefly because it can
o: be blended into blast-furnace slag to make low-carbon cement
replace limestone as the flux that removes impurities from molten iron
be used as a coolant in continuous casting of steel
serve as the reducing gas in making Direct Reduced Iron, partly replacing imported coking coal and natural gas
questions.e: Iron ore is iron oxide, and making iron means removing the oxygen. In the direct-reduction route this is done by a hot reducing gas, and the carbon monoxide and hydrogen in syngas can do that job. India imports most of its coking coal and much of its gas, so this is an import-substitution argument. The other three uses have nothing to do with the chemistry of syngas.

questions.q:
With reference to India's water resources, consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Of the roughly 4,000 billion cubic metres of precipitation India receives in a year, only a little over a quarter is usable.
Statement-II: India is the world's largest user of groundwater, accounting for about a quarter of global extraction.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both statements are correct, but the second does not explain the first. The gap between rainfall and usable water arises from limited storage, uneven distribution over space and season, and the need to leave water for ecosystems. Heavy groundwater pumping is a separate fact: it is how farms cope with unreliable surface supply, and it causes falling water tables. Together they show a governance problem more than a shortage of rain.

questions.q:
Scientists are using 'DNA maps' to trace pangolin trafficking hubs. With reference to pangolins, consider the following statements:
1. They are the only mammals fully covered in scales made of keratin.
2. They have no teeth and feed mainly on ants and termites.
3. Both species found in India occur throughout the North-Eastern States.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Pangolins are solitary, nocturnal and toothless, catch insects with a long sticky tongue, and roll into a ball when threatened; their scales drive the illegal trade. Statement 3 is wrong. Of eight species worldwide two occur in India: the Indian pangolin is found over most of the country south of the Himalayas but not in most of the North-East, where the Chinese pangolin takes over.

questions.q:
With reference to species in the news in May 2026, consider the following pairs:
Species : IUCN status
1. Asiatic cheetah : Critically Endangered
2. Indian pangolin : Endangered
3. Chinese pangolin : Vulnerable
4. Indian soft-shell turtle : Least Concern
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1 and 2 are correct. The Asiatic cheetah survives only in Iran and is Critically Endangered, while the African cheetah brought to India is Vulnerable. The Indian pangolin is Endangered. Pair 3 is wrong: the Chinese pangolin, found in Assam and the eastern Himalayas, is Critically Endangered. Pair 4 is wrong: the Indian or Ganges soft-shell turtle is Endangered and, like both pangolins, is in Schedule I and CITES Appendix I.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. La Nina is marked by warmer-than-normal sea surface temperatures in the eastern equatorial Pacific.
2. During El Nino the Walker circulation strengthens, bringing heavier rain to Indonesia and northern Australia.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Neither is correct. La Nina is the cool phase: stronger trade winds pile warm water in the west and bring cold water up in the east, and India usually gets more rain. In El Nino the Walker circulation weakens or shifts east, so Indonesia and Australia turn dry while the coast of Peru gets rain. A third, neutral phase lies between the two. The droughts of 2002 and 2009 in India were El Nino years.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 74-75; Walker circulation is static

questions.q:
With reference to the Global Forest Goals Report 2026, consider the following statements:
1. It is brought out by the UN Department of Economic and Social Affairs with the Secretariat of the UN Forum on Forests.
2. The Global Forest Goals are legally binding on the member States of the United Nations.
3. The goals form part of the UN Strategic Plan for Forests, which runs up to 2030.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. The Forum on Forests, set up in 2000, is an intergovernmental body of all UN members, and its strategic plan for 2017 to 2030 contains six goals, from reversing forest loss to better finance and governance. Statement 2 is wrong: the goals and their targets are voluntary. The 2026 report found that forest area had shrunk since 2015 and that finance was far below need.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 82-83; voluntary nature is static

questions.q: A 'heat dome', which scorched parts of western Europe in 2026, is best described as
o: a low-pressure trough that draws hot desert air towards the coast
a layer of warm air trapped over a city by its buildings and paved surfaces
a mass of hot air that descends the leeward side of a mountain range
a persistent high-pressure system under which sinking air is compressed and warmed, and clouds are suppressed
questions.e: Under a stalled high-pressure ridge, air sinks, is compressed and warms; clear skies let more sunshine reach the ground, and the hot air cannot escape, bulging upward like a dome. The result is a long heatwave with drought and fire risk. The urban heat island is a local city effect, and warm descending wind on a lee slope is a foehn-type wind; neither is a heat dome.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about measures suggested for a reliable renewable-led grid:
1. Ancillary services markets procure services such as reserves and frequency support needed to balance the grid.
2. Green Energy Corridors are transmission projects meant to evacuate power from renewable-rich States.
3. Pumped hydro stores energy by lifting water to an upper reservoir when power is in surplus.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: All three are correct. Ancillary services keep frequency stable when supply or demand changes suddenly, which matters more as variable sources grow. Green Energy Corridors link renewable-rich States such as Rajasthan and Gujarat with demand centres. Pumped hydro works like a large battery, releasing the stored water through turbines at peak hours. These measures, with market reform and a phased retirement of inefficient coal units, are the systemic changes the transition needs.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 52-54; definitions are static

questions.q: 'SEHAT' (Science Excellence for Health through Agricultural Transformation), launched in 2026, is a joint initiative of the
o: Indian Council of Medical Research and the Indian Council of Agricultural Research
NITI Aayog and the World Health Organization
Indian Council of Agricultural Research and the Food and Agriculture Organization
Department of Biotechnology and the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
questions.e: The two research councils, one for medicine and one for agriculture, launched the initiative to make farming a driver of nutrition and health and not only of food output. Its priorities are biofortified crops, integrated farming systems, health risks of farm workers, functional foods against non-communicable diseases, and One Health preparedness. The idea is preventive: tackle under-nutrition and diet-related disease together through what is grown and eaten.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
1. Ocean alkalinity enhancement
2. Artificial upwelling
3. Sinking of biomass in the deep sea
4. Stratospheric aerosol injection
How many of the above are approaches to marine carbon dioxide removal?
questions.e: The first three are marine removal methods: they raise the ocean's capacity to take up carbon dioxide or move carbon to the deep sea. Restoring mangroves and seagrass is another. Stratospheric aerosol injection belongs to a different family, solar radiation management, which reflects sunlight and leaves carbon dioxide where it is. Both are loosely called geoengineering, which is why they are confused. Removal supplements emission cuts and cannot replace them.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 70-71; solar radiation management is static

questions.q: The definition of ecocide proposed in 2021 differs from the environmental war-crime threshold in the Rome Statute in that the proposed definition
o: covers only damage that injures or displaces human beings
makes States, and not individuals or companies, criminally liable
applies only during armed conflict, whereas the Rome Statute provision also applies in peacetime
requires severe damage that is either widespread or long-term, instead of requiring all three features together
questions.e: The proposed definition speaks of unlawful or wanton acts done knowing there is a substantial likelihood of severe and either widespread or long-term damage. The Rome Statute's wording joins the three features with 'and', which is far harder to prove. The proposal would also apply in peacetime and treats the environment itself as the victim, departing from the human-centred approach of existing law. Liability would fall on individuals, including company decision-makers.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Antarctic sea ice has declined abruptly since about 2015.
Statement-II: Stronger westerly winds have drawn warm, salty deep water of the Southern Ocean towards the surface.
Statement-III: The melting of floating sea ice raises global sea level substantially, which in turn submerges and melts more ice.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-II and Statement-III are correct and both of them explain Statement-I
Both Statement-II and Statement-III are correct but only one of them explains Statement-I
Only one of the Statements II and III is correct and that explains Statement-I
Neither Statement-II nor Statement-III is correct
questions.e: Statement-II is correct and explains the decline. A layer of cold, fresh water used to keep deep-ocean heat away from the surface; westerlies strengthened by the ozone hole and greenhouse gases have pulled that deep water up. It brings heat that melts ice and salt that makes mixing easier, a self-reinforcing loop. Statement-III is wrong: sea ice already floats, so its melting barely changes sea level, unlike loss of grounded ice.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 84; sea-level point is static

questions.q: In the circular-economy debate of May 2026, a limitation pointed out in India's e-waste and battery-waste rules was that they
o: apply to importers of electronic goods but exempt domestic manufacturers
prescribe collection targets for consumers instead of placing responsibility on producers
permit landfilling of lithium-ion batteries where recycling units are not available
mainly reward recovery of high-value metals such as gold, copper and aluminium and leave out a wider basket of critical minerals
questions.e: The criticism is about what the rules incentivise. Recyclers go after gold, copper and aluminium because targets and economics favour them, while lithium, cobalt, rare earths and similar minerals are poorly recovered. The rules do bind domestic producers, they rest on producer responsibility rather than consumer targets, and the battery rules bar landfilling. The National Critical Mineral Mission, 2025 tries to fill this gap by building recycling capacity.

questions.q:
With reference to the El Nino-Southern Oscillation, in the news because of a forecast for late 2026, consider the following statements:
1. El Nino is the warm phase of the oscillation and is associated with weaker trade winds over the equatorial Pacific.
2. 'Super El Nino' is a formal category of the World Meteorological Organization.
3. In El Nino Modoki the warming is centred in the central Pacific and not off South America.
4. A positive Indian Ocean Dipole, with a warmer western Indian Ocean, can partly offset El Nino's effect on the monsoon.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. In El Nino the trade winds slacken and warm water spreads east, shifting rainfall away from the Indian side. Modoki is the central-Pacific variety and can also weaken the monsoon. A positive dipole favours convection near India, as happened in some El Nino years with near-normal rain. Statement 2 is wrong: 'super' is an informal label for exceptionally strong events.

questions.q: Ocean alkalinity enhancement, discussed in 2026 as a method of marine carbon dioxide removal, works by
o: adding alkaline material so that more dissolved carbon dioxide is held as bicarbonate, allowing the sea to absorb more from the air
cooling the sea surface so that gases dissolve more readily in it
fertilising surface water with iron so that plankton blooms take up carbon
pumping liquefied carbon dioxide into depleted oil wells beneath the seabed
questions.e: Adding alkaline minerals shifts seawater chemistry so that dissolved carbon dioxide is converted to bicarbonate and carbonate, which are stable for very long periods. The surface water can then draw more of the gas from the air, and the acidity of the water falls. Iron fertilisation is a separate biological method, seabed injection is geological storage, and cooling is not what the method does. Verifying how much carbon is removed is the main difficulty.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 70-71; ocean chemistry is static

questions.q:
In the context of India's position on ecocide, consider the following statements:
1. India has signed the Rome Statute but has not ratified it.
2. The Ecocide (Prevention and Accountability) Bill, 2025 is a Government Bill pending in the Lok Sabha.
3. India has no distinct offence of ecocide and relies on laws such as the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 and the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 3 is correct. India has neither signed nor ratified the Rome Statute, so statement 1 is wrong. The 2025 Bill is a Private Member's Bill in the Rajya Sabha that would make ecocide an offence for individuals and companies; such Bills rarely become law. India instead uses a patchwork of environmental statutes, the criminal code and the National Green Tribunal, along with the right to a clean environment read into Article 21.

questions.q: It is said that fossil fuels 'set the marginal cost' of electricity, so that even domestically generated power is exposed to global fuel shocks. This is because
o: renewable plants have higher running costs than coal plants and are therefore dispatched last
electricity tariffs in India are legally indexed to the international price of crude oil
the price in a power market is fixed by the costliest plant needed to meet demand, which is usually a fossil-fuel plant
most of the coal burnt in Indian power plants is imported through the Strait of Hormuz
questions.e: Plants are dispatched in order of running cost. Solar and wind have almost no fuel cost and go first; the last plant needed to meet demand, typically coal or gas, sets the price for that period. When fuel prices jump because of trouble in West Asia, that marginal price rises for everyone. Tariffs are not indexed to crude, and what passes through Hormuz is mainly oil and LNG, not power-station coal.

questions.q:
Cheetahs from Botswana were released in Kuno National Park in 2026. In this context, consider the following statements:
1. Like the lion and the tiger, the cheetah can roar.
2. In the wild, the Asiatic cheetah now survives only in Iran.
3. Project Cheetah is implemented by the Wildlife Institute of India, which is the statutory authority for it.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 2 is correct. Cheetahs cannot roar; they purr and chirp, unlike lions, tigers, leopards and jaguars. The Asiatic subspecies is confined to arid eastern Iran, which is why India turned to African cheetahs. The project, begun in 2022 as the first intercontinental translocation of a large wild carnivore, is implemented by the National Tiger Conservation Authority. The cheetah was declared extinct in India in 1952.

questions.q:
According to figures cited with the Global Forest Goals Report 2026, five countries hold more than half of the world's forests. Which of the following are among them?
1. Russia
2. Brazil
3. Indonesia
4. Canada
5. Democratic Republic of the Congo
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: The five are Russia, Brazil, Canada, the United States and China, together holding about 54 per cent of global forest area, with Russia alone at a fifth. Indonesia and the Democratic Republic of the Congo have large tropical rainforests and figure in deforestation debates, but they are not in the top five by area. Forests cover about 32 per cent of the world's land, and tropical forests are the largest climatic group.

questions.q: The Chungthang dam, cited in May 2026 discussions on dam safety as an example of risk from glacial lake outburst floods, stood on the
questions.e: The Chungthang dam of the Teesta-III project in north Sikkim was washed away in October 2023 when South Lhonak Lake burst and sent a flood down the Teesta. The Rangit is a tributary of the Teesta in the same State and has its own project, which makes it the closest distractor. The Subansiri and Dhauliganga have hydropower projects but were not the site of this failure.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 72-74; river and location are static

questions.q:
With reference to water institutions in India, consider the following statements:
1. The Central Ground Water Authority regulates groundwater extraction by industry through No Objection Certificates.
2. The Central Ground Water Authority was constituted under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.
3. The Central Water Commission is the body responsible for groundwater assessment and aquifer management.
4. The Central Pollution Control Board owes its creation to the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. The groundwater authority was set up under Section 3(3) of the 1986 Act and works through NOCs for industry and infrastructure. The 1974 Water Act created the central and State pollution control boards. Statement 3 is wrong: the Central Water Commission handles surface water, river-basin planning and flood control, while groundwater assessment belongs to the Central Ground Water Board.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 47-48; CGWA's constitution under the 1986 Act is static

questions.q: Parametric insurance is emerging in India as cover against heatwaves. Which one of the following is a characteristic limitation of such insurance?
o: The payout may not match the loss actually suffered, since it depends on an index crossing a trigger
Claims take long to settle because each loss must be surveyed
It can be offered only by government-owned insurers
It cannot cover weather events, as these lack measurable parameters
questions.e: A parametric policy pays a pre-agreed sum when a measured value, such as temperature, rainfall or wind speed, crosses a set threshold. No loss survey is needed, so money reaches people fast, which is its main merit over indemnity insurance. The price of that speed is basis risk: a household may suffer loss without the trigger being hit, or be paid without loss. Weather is in fact the commonest use of such cover.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 84-85; basis risk is static

questions.q:
With reference to 'ecocide', which was in the news in May 2026 after a report by Lebanon, consider the following statements:
1. The term was coined in the context of herbicide use during the Vietnam War.
2. A motion recognising ecocide adopted by the IUCN in 2025 does not create binding legal liability.
3. It is listed as the fifth core crime in the Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The plant biologist Arthur Galston coined the word in 1970 while protesting against defoliants in Vietnam. The IUCN motion of 2025 recognises ecocide as a concept, but a resolution of a conservation body binds no one; the first binding treaty in this field is the Council of Europe's 2025 convention. Statement 3 is wrong. The Rome Statute has four core crimes: genocide, crimes against humanity, war crimes and aggression. Adding ecocide as a fifth is a campaign demand, not the law.

questions.q: El Nino was named by Peruvian fishermen, who noticed its effects around Christmas. Which one of the following explains why their catch falls in an El Nino year?
o: Heavier trade winds make the sea too rough for coastal fishing.
Salinity off Peru rises sharply because rainfall on the coast fails.
Warm surface water spreads east and suppresses the upwelling of cold, nutrient-rich water off Peru.
The Humboldt Current strengthens and carries fish northwards towards the Equator.
questions.e: Normally trade winds push surface water west, and cold water rich in nutrients rises along the Peruvian coast, feeding plankton and one of the world's great anchovy fisheries. In El Nino the winds weaken, warm water moves in and the thermocline deepens, so nutrients no longer reach the surface. The cold Humboldt Current weakens, trade winds are lighter, and coastal Peru gets more rain, not less.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 74-75; upwelling is static

questions.q:
With reference to the two AI-enabled forecast products launched in May 2026, consider the following statements:
1. The forecast of monsoon advance is probabilistic, issued weekly and looks up to four weeks ahead.
2. The pilot for Uttar Pradesh gives rainfall forecasts at a resolution of one kilometre using AI-driven downscaling.
3. Both were developed by the Indian Council of Agricultural Research for the agriculture ministry.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The monsoon-advance product, the first of its kind, combines AI models with extended-range prediction and reaches farmers through the agriculture ministry's network. The Uttar Pradesh pilot blends rain gauges, weather stations, Doppler radars and satellite data and looks ten days ahead. Statement 3 is wrong: the Ministry of Earth Sciences launched them, and they were built by the weather department, IITM Pune and the medium-range forecasting centre.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about capacity building for dam safety in India:
1. International Centres of Excellence for Dams have been set up at IIT Roorkee and IISc Bengaluru.
2. The National Centre for Earthquake Safety of Dams is located at IIT Roorkee.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct; the two centres of excellence support research, training and advisory work for dam owners. Statement 2 is wrong: the earthquake safety centre is at MNIT Jaipur and works on seismic hazard mapping and risk assessment. Seismic risk is real, as the 2001 Bhuj earthquake caused liquefaction in the foundation of the Chang dam in Gujarat. About a quarter of India's specified dams are over fifty years old.

questions.q:
The 17th Petersberg Climate Dialogue in 2026 reaffirmed multilateral climate action. In this context, consider the following statements:
1. The Global Environment Facility serves as a financial mechanism for the UN conventions on climate change, biological diversity and desertification.
2. The Green Climate Fund was set up under the UN climate convention by a decision taken at Cancun in 2010.
3. The principle of common but differentiated responsibilities appears in the text of the UN climate convention.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: All three are correct. The Global Environment Facility, set up in 1991, funds several conventions, including the three Rio conventions. The Green Climate Fund was created at the Cancun conference and is the convention's dedicated climate fund. Differentiated responsibility is written into Article 3 of the 1992 convention and is the basis of climate-justice claims. Developed countries' delay in meeting the 100-billion-dollar pledge weakened trust in this system.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 78-79; fund and treaty details are static

questions.q: India's first satellite-tagged Indian soft-shell turtle was released in 2026 in
questions.e: The turtle was tagged and released in Kaziranga in Assam, on the Brahmaputra floodplain. The species is a freshwater turtle of the Indus, Ganga, Narmada, Mahanadi and Brahmaputra basins, recognised by arrowhead marks on its head. Chambal is known for gharials and other river turtles, while Bhitarkanika and the Sundarbans are estuarine habitats associated with olive ridley and river terrapin, so they are the plausible but wrong choices.

questions.q:
With reference to fuel standards issued by the Bureau of Indian Standards in 2026, consider the following statements:
1. Dimethyl ether, for whose blends with LPG a standard was issued, can be made from syngas either through methanol or directly.
2. The new standard for ethanol-blended petrol stops at E20, the level already reached under the Ethanol Blended Petrol programme.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: the indirect route makes methanol first and then dehydrates it, while the direct route goes from syngas to the ether in one step. China holds most of the world's capacity. Statement 2 is wrong. Since 20 per cent blending has been achieved, the new standard covers higher blends, E22, E25, E27 and E30, using anhydrous ethanol with motor gasoline, preparing the ground for blending beyond E20.

questions.q: Which one of the following is not correct about the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026?
o: Local bodies that send unsegregated waste to landfills face higher landfill fees.
They were framed by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs under the municipal laws of the States.
Local bodies are encouraged to generate carbon credits from waste management.
Material Recovery Facilities serve as deposition points for streams such as e-waste and sanitary waste.
questions.e: The rules were notified by the environment ministry under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, replacing the 2016 rules from 1 April 2026; they do not rest on State municipal laws. The other three are provisions of the rules: carbon credits for local bodies, recognised sorting facilities that also receive special streams, and a fee penalty meant to push source segregation and cut dependence on landfills.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 51-52; Vision IAS p. 66

questions.q:
With reference to geothermal energy in India, consider the following statements:
1. High-enthalpy resources are used for direct heating, whereas low-enthalpy resources are used to generate electricity.
2. The Puga and Chumathang fields, regarded as the most promising in the country, lie in Ladakh.
3. The pilot plant in the Puga Valley is to be built by NTPC.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 reverses the rule: high-enthalpy sources in volcanic or hot-spring regions drive turbines, while low and medium-enthalpy heat is used directly for heating, cooling, farming and aquaculture. Statement 3 names the wrong company; ONGC is to build the one-megawatt pilot under a memorandum with the Ladakh administration, which was extended in 2026. A national geothermal policy was issued in 2025.

questions.q:
Prosopis juliflora is to be the feedstock for India's first green methanol plant. In this context, consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Where it invades, Prosopis juliflora worsens hydrological drought.
Statement-II: It is a leguminous tree native to the Americas that tolerates drought and salinity.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both statements are correct, but the second is not the reason for the first. The plant worsens drought because it is a phreatophyte: its deep roots reach below the water table and draw groundwater continuously. Its legume character and tolerance of salt explain why it was planted, in Delhi in the 1920s and in Gujarat in 1961, and why it spreads. Using it as fuel feedstock turns an invasive into a resource.

questions.q:
With reference to the Dam Rehabilitation and Improvement Project (DRIP), consider the following statements:
1. Its first phase was supported by the World Bank.
2. Its second and third phases are co-financed by the World Bank and the Asian Development Bank.
3. Maharashtra has the largest number of specified dams in India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is right: the first phase ran from 2012 to 2021 with World Bank support and covered dams in seven States. Statement 2 is wrong because the co-financier of the later phases is the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank, not the Asian Development Bank. Statement 3 is right; Maharashtra leads, followed by Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat. Almost all specified dams belong to State governments, so States carry the maintenance burden.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs relating to downstream use of syngas:
Process : Product
1. Methanation : Ammonia
2. Fischer-Tropsch synthesis : Liquid hydrocarbon fuels
3. Dehydration of methanol : Dimethyl ether
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pair 1 is wrong: methanation combines carbon monoxide and hydrogen into methane, giving synthetic natural gas. Ammonia is made by reacting the hydrogen from syngas with nitrogen. Pair 2 is right; Fischer-Tropsch chemistry builds liquid hydrocarbons from syngas. Pair 3 is right and is the indirect route to dimethyl ether, a clean-burning fuel that behaves much like LPG and for whose LPG blends a standard was issued in 2026.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 68-70; Vision IAS p. 81; process chemistry is static

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the Global Methane Pledge is correct?
o: It covers methane from oil and gas operations only and excludes agriculture and waste.
It was launched at COP27 along with the Methane Alert and Response System, with India as a founding participant.
It is a voluntary collective commitment to cut global methane emissions by at least 30 per cent from 2020 levels by 2030.
It is a legally binding protocol under the Paris Agreement with country-wise methane targets.
questions.e: The pledge was launched at COP26 in 2021, led by the United States and the European Union. It is voluntary and the 30 per cent target is collective, not national. It covers all sources, including farming and waste. India has stayed out, mainly because its methane comes from livestock and paddy grown by small farmers. The satellite alert system launched at COP27 helps participants locate large leaks.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 79-80; India's non-participation is static

questions.q:
With reference to international law on environmental destruction, consider the following pairs:
Instrument or body : Feature
1. ENMOD Convention : Bars hostile use of techniques that manipulate natural processes, such as weather modification
2. Rome Statute : Treats grave environmental damage as punishable only when it is a war crime
3. Council of Europe convention of 2025 on protecting the environment through criminal law : First binding international treaty to criminalise severe, large-scale environmental destruction
4. Stop Ecocide International : Non-profit behind the 2021 proposed legal definition of ecocide
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: All four pairs are correct. The ENMOD Convention deals with using the environment as a weapon. The Rome Statute covers environmental harm only inside its war-crimes article, so peacetime industrial destruction falls outside. The Council of Europe treaty is the first binding instrument on conduct often called ecocide and lets European courts try acts done abroad. The 2021 definition came from an expert panel convened by a non-profit, and has no official status.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: In May 2026 the Material Recycling Association of India sought a single nodal agency or dedicated ministry for the circular economy.
Statement-II: Waste regulation in India is framed by the environment ministry while urban planning and municipal implementation lie with the housing and urban affairs ministry.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both statements are correct and the second gives the reason for the first. Responsibility for waste is split: the environment ministry writes the rules, the urban affairs ministry and local bodies carry them out, and several other regulators handle individual waste streams. The recyclers' body argued that this fragmentation, along with weak traceability and data, needs one institutional anchor. NITI Aayog's cell coordinates but does not regulate.

questions.q: Which one of the following correctly states the difference between a carbon tax and an emissions trading system?
o: A tax is permitted under the Paris Agreement, whereas a trading system requires approval under its Article 6.
A tax applies to producers of fossil fuels, whereas a trading system applies to consumers of electricity.
A tax raises revenue for the government, whereas a trading system can never raise any.
A tax fixes the price of emissions and lets the quantity adjust, whereas a trading system fixes the quantity or intensity and lets the price be discovered.
questions.e: Both put a price on carbon but from opposite ends. A tax gives price certainty and leaves the amount of abatement to firms. A trading system sets a cap, or in India's case an emission-intensity target for each obligated entity, and the market sets the price of allowances or credits. Trading systems raise revenue when allowances are auctioned. Neither needs clearance under the Paris Agreement; Article 6 concerns cross-border transfers.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 80; the distinction is static

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The River Boards Act, 1956 was enacted by Parliament under Article 262 of the Constitution.
Statement-II: Article 262 allows Parliament to provide by law that neither the Supreme Court nor any other court shall exercise jurisdiction over an inter-State river water dispute.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is incorrect. The River Boards Act draws on Entry 56 of the Union List, which covers regulation and development of inter-State rivers, and it allows only advisory boards. Statement-II is correct: Article 262 deals with adjudication of disputes and permits Parliament to oust court jurisdiction, which it did through the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act of the same year. The two 1956 laws are easily confused.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 47-48; Article 262 is static

questions.q:
With reference to the International Big Cat Alliance, consider the following statements:
1. Its membership is confined to countries in which big cats occur naturally.
2. It was launched in 2023 to mark fifty years of Project Tiger and is headquartered in India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is wrong. The alliance is open to range countries and also to non-range countries interested in big-cat conservation, as well as partner organisations; Saudi Arabia joined in 2026. Statement 2 is right. India launched it on the fiftieth anniversary of Project Tiger, hosts its headquarters and provided the initial budget support. It shares practices, expertise and funds for seven big cats, which act as keystone species.

questions.q:
The Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 were framed under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986. In this context, consider the following pairs:
Law : Constitutional route used by Parliament
1. Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 : Article 253, to give effect to the Stockholm Declaration
2. Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974 : Article 252, on resolutions passed by State Legislatures
3. Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981 : Article 253, to give effect to the Stockholm Declaration
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: All three pairs are correct. Water is a State subject, so the 1974 Water Act needed resolutions of State Legislatures under Article 252. By 1981 and 1986 Parliament relied instead on Article 253, which lets it legislate on any subject to implement an international decision, here the 1972 Stockholm Conference on the Human Environment. This is why the Centre can frame waste rules even though local government is a State subject.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 51-52; Vision IAS p. 66; constitutional basis of the Water and Air Acts is static

questions.q: In M.K. Ranjitsinh vs Union of India (2024), cited in the ecocide debate, the Supreme Court recognised a right to be free from the adverse effects of climate change. The Court derived this right from
questions.e: The case was about protecting the Great Indian Bustard from overhead power lines in Rajasthan and Gujarat while allowing renewable energy to expand. The Court held that climate harm threatens life and health under Article 21 and falls unequally on vulnerable groups, engaging equality under Article 14. Articles 48A and 51A(g) are a Directive Principle and a Fundamental Duty; they guide interpretation but are not themselves enforceable fundamental rights.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 49-50; the Articles relied on are static

questions.q:
With reference to oversight under the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026, consider the following statements:
1. Landfills are to be audited every year by the Central Pollution Control Board.
2. The State-level implementation committee is chaired by the Chief Secretary, or the head of the Union Territory.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is wrong: the annual landfill audit is the job of the State Pollution Control Boards, while District Collectors oversee landfill performance. The central board's role is the online portal and dashboards. Statement 2 is right; the rules create Central and State committees, and the State one sits under the Chief Secretary. Critics say this still leaves States working inside a centrally written rulebook.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 51-52; Vision IAS p. 66

questions.q: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes biomass gasification from anaerobic digestion, the two technologies of decentralised bioenergy?
o: Gasification works on wet waste in the absence of oxygen, while digestion burns dry residues with limited air.
Both yield a gas made mainly of methane, but only digestion can be used at village scale.
Gasification is a biological process carried out by microbes, while digestion is a thermo-chemical process.
Gasification turns dry residues such as husk and stalks into producer gas, while digestion turns wet waste such as manure and food scraps into biogas.
questions.e: Gasification is thermo-chemical: dry biomass is heated with limited air to give producer gas, a mix rich in carbon monoxide and hydrogen, used in small engines and for industrial heat. Anaerobic digestion is biological: microbes break down wet organic matter without oxygen to give methane-rich biogas for cooking and power. Both suit village or cluster scale, which is why they are proposed as a hedge against volatile fuel supply chains.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Mission)
A. Atal Bhujal Yojana
B. AMRUT
C. Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana
D. Namami Gange
List-II (Main focus)
1. Pollution abatement and ecological restoration of a river basin
2. Community-led groundwater budgeting in water-stressed areas
3. Urban water supply, sewage treatment and reuse of wastewater
4. Micro-irrigation and better on-farm water management
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Atal Bhujal Yojana works on the demand side of groundwater, asking communities to prepare water budgets and monitor aquifers. AMRUT is the urban mission for water supply, sewerage and reuse. The irrigation scheme promotes drip and sprinkler systems since farming uses most of India's freshwater. Namami Gange restores the Ganga basin through sewage treatment and ecological work. Central funds flow through these missions while States implement them.

questions.q: Which one of the following is not correct with reference to the findings and figures of the Global Forest Goals Report 2026?
o: Boreal forests make up the largest share of the world's forest area.
World forest area fell between 2015 and 2025.
Expansion of agriculture and demand for fuelwood and charcoal are the main drivers of forest loss.
Finance for forests is well below what is needed each year by 2030.
questions.e: Tropical forests are the largest group, at about 45 per cent of forest area; boreal forests come second, followed by temperate and subtropical. The other three statements reflect the report: more than 40 million hectares were lost in a decade, farming and fuelwood demand lead the causes, and forest finance, though at a record level in 2023, is under a third of the annual requirement. Clean cooking energy is therefore a forest measure too.

questions.q:
With reference to small hydro power in India, consider the following statements:
1. Run-of-the-river projects generate power from the natural flow of a river without large dams or storage.
2. Only about a quarter of the country's identified small-hydro potential has been harnessed so far.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both are correct. Run-of-the-river design avoids large reservoirs, which keeps displacement and submergence low and suits hilly and remote areas. Identified potential is about 21,000 MW across more than 7,000 sites, of which roughly 5,000 MW is installed. The northern region holds the largest share, with Himachal Pradesh leading. The new scheme aims to add about 1,500 MW, mainly in hill, North-Eastern and border areas.
